scope: Theorem 3.1 (The one-sign component inequality) of the manuscript “The nonmaximal anti-de Sitter Penrose Inequality and original-data rigidity” (preprints/The-nonmaximal-anti-de-Sitter-Penrose-Inequality-and-original-data-rigidity-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9e2b9ba2768918dc), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 10. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let (Ω, g, K) satisfy Definition 2.1, and assume H + trTS K ≤ 0 on every component of S, with the convention of Equation (2.5). Suppose that K is compactly supported and that one of the two tensors K − (trg K)g, −K + (trg K)g is positive semidefinite throughout Ω. In each fixed admissible hyperbolic chart for which the metric fluxes exist, p0(g) ≥ s Ag(S) 16π + 1 2  Ag(S) 4π 3/2 . (3.1) This assertion does not require the flux covector to be timelike. If that covector is future timelike, its Lorentz norm satisfies the same lower bound.
